# How the typescript parser decides

<!-- generated by `npm run gen` from the portable plan (src/emit-portable.ts) of `typescript.ts`; do not edit by hand. -->

Every choice point of the grammar and how the generated parser (the portable plan every target prints) decides it: by one token, by two tokens, by attempt (an ordered choice tries its branches in order; a repetition without a FIRST guard tries its body), or by longest match in a candidate frame; and whether it takes a mark that a failure restores. Then the findings a grammar author should act on, each with its witness and a suggested action. How it is derived: src/decision-report.ts.

## Findings

### Dead alternatives

It always matches exactly one token, and at every token it admits a candidate declared before it is surely tried and matches at least that token: the earlier one wins the tie, so this one never wins. For the root grammars `node test/decision-report.ts --dead` removes each from the grammar and requires that no tree on the corpora changes.

| list | dead alternative | taken by | at | witness | action |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Type NUD | true_ (#20) | ident (#0) | `true` | `true` as Type | remove the arm, or declare it before `ident` / guard `ident`: `ident`, declared before it, takes every input it could match |
| Type NUD | false_ (#21) | ident (#0) | `false` | `false` as Type | remove the arm, or declare it before `ident` / guard `ident`: `ident`, declared before it, takes every input it could match |
| Type NUD | null_ (#22) | ident (#0) | `null` | `null` as Type | remove the arm, or declare it before `ident` / guard `ident`: `ident`, declared before it, takes every input it could match |
| Type NUD | undefined (#23) | ident (#0) | `undefined` | `undefined` as Type | remove the arm, or declare it before `ident` / guard `ident`: `ident`, declared before it, takes every input it could match |
| Type NUD | void_ (#24) | ident (#0) | `void` | `void` as Type | remove the arm, or declare it before `ident` / guard `ident`: `ident`, declared before it, takes every input it could match |

### Ties decided by declaration order

Two candidates of one list match the same input to the same end; the one declared first wins. Where the later one is meant to win there, the grammar must say so (reorder, or refuse the token in the earlier one). "One token": both can match exactly one token at these tokens (the witness is that token parsed as the rule, where the engine observes the tie). "Observed": a frame on the pinned inputs where they tied (how often, and the first place).

| list | wins (declared first) | loses | one token | observed | witness | action |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|--:|:--|:--|
| Decl | declare (#9) | declared (#12) |  | 11 | typescript/lib/lib.es5.d.ts:33: `declare function eval(x: string): any;` | reorder, or guard `declare`: the tie of declare and declared is resolved only by declaration order (declare wins) |
| Type NUD | ident (#0) | this_ (#25) | `this` | 189 | typescript/lib/typescript.d.ts:9338: `this;` | reorder, or guard `ident`: the tie of ident and this_ on `this` is resolved only by declaration order (ident wins) |
| TypeMember | new_ (#0) | seq2 (#2) |  | 70 | typescript/lib/lib.es5.d.ts:156: `new (value?: any): Object;` | reorder, or guard `new_`: the tie of new_ and seq2 is resolved only by declaration order (new_ wins) |

None.
